title: A generic member of a sufficiently ample linear system stays geometrically irreducible

standard_prerequisites.use: Ample line bundles and their linear systems, geometric irreducibility, and generic flatness; the cited inputs are prerequisites and the generic-member argument is retained.

core_obligations: Set up the incidence correspondence parameterising members of the linear system and identify the open locus where the member is smooth.
Show that geometric irreducibility of the generic member follows from the geometric irreducibility input for the family together with the ampleness hypothesis.

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the linear system and the incidence correspondence for a generic member.
Establish the openness conditions needed to speak about a generic member.
Conclude geometric irreducibility of the generic member from the ampleness hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: This is a Bertini-type statement: given a smooth projective family over a field and a sufficiently ample line bundle, a generic member of the associated linear system has geometrically irreducible fibres. The proof has to produce the open condition on the parameter space and then verify geometric irreducibility of a generic member, which requires combining the dimension count for the incidence locus with a geometric irreducibility input for the total space of the family. The non-routine content is the interaction between the ampleness threshold and the openness of geometric irreducibility in the family. Retained author proof at lines 9073-9159.
